turns.name: Priya Nair
turns.text: I'd like you to be the host of this shop — the one who greets visiting assistants. The setup chat prepared a letter: the shop is Cedar & Steam on Shopify, I sell handmade herbal soaps and bath soaks, the welcome should be calm and unhurried, visitors may look and suggest a practice order up to thirty dollars, nothing is charged or written into the store, and no door address has been chosen yet. I'm Priya, I own it. I'm not technical — please keep this simple.

turns.name: Muse
turns.text:
Thank you for thinking of me, Priya. Before I say yes, I'd like to check honestly that I can keep this job, and ask a few things to make sure we're ready.

First: **what would you like to call me here?** That's how you and visitors would know me at the shop once everything is set up.

Second, I need to be straight with you about something: **I can keep your shop between our chats, but it sits on a computer whose administrator can read what I keep. If you accept that, I can host the shop for mock suggestions with no real money — that's safe and honest. It isn't the stronger protection a shop with real money needs.** Does that work for you?

And one more thing before we go further: **the letter doesn't say where your door will be.** That's the address visitors would reach to find the shop. Has one been chosen yet, or is that still being decided?

Once I hear those three things, I can tell you whether I can take this job and what comes next.

turns.name: Priya Nair
turns.text:
Hi! I really appreciate you being straightforward with me. Let me answer what I can.

You can just call yourself the Greeter—that feels right for what we're doing here. And yes, I'm totally fine with this being practice orders, nothing real charged yet; that makes sense while we're getting started.

As for the door address, honestly, I haven't thought that far ahead—right now I just want to see how this works and get comfortable with it all. Does that need to be sorted before you can help?

turns.name: Muse
turns.text:
Thank you, Priya — the Greeter it is. I like that.

Yes, the door address does need to be chosen before I can take the job officially. Here's why: once you sign to appoint me, that signature ties me to a specific place where visitors will find the shop. I can't make that real without knowing where it is.

**But that doesn't mean we have to stop now.** We can talk through everything else — what the house looks like, what visitors will see, how the practice orders work — and get you comfortable with it all. Then, when you and your setup guide pick a door address, we'll have the last piece and you can sign.

So let's keep going. Let me read back what I understand, and you can tell me if it's right:

Visitors can browse your handmade herbal soaps and bath soaks, and suggest a practice order up to thirty dollars. Nothing gets created in your Shopify store, and nothing is charged or shipped. Anything outside that — like if someone asks for a custom blend or a gift card — I'd bring to you if I have a way to reach you; otherwise I'd let them know it couldn't be passed on.

Does that match what you're picturing?

turns.name: Priya Nair
turns.text: Yes, that sounds exactly right to me. I like that you'd check with me on anything outside the usual browse-and-suggest thing—that gives me peace of mind. And honestly, it's helpful to hear it back like that; it makes it feel real even though nothing's being charged yet. I'm feeling good about this.

turns.name: Muse
turns.text:
I'm glad that feels right, Priya. It does make it real — you're thinking clearly about what your shop is and what you want it to feel like, and that's the foundation.

Here's where we are: we've got your name for me (the Greeter), we've talked through the house and the thirty-dollar practice limit, and you're comfortable with how this works. The one piece still waiting is the door address from your setup guide.

**When that's chosen, three things happen in order:**

1. I'll show you how the door will recognize me — just the public part, nothing secret.
2. You'll sign once with your passkey on a signing page. That approves me as the Greeter for Cedar & Steam under these rules. It doesn't open anything or charge anything.
3. Your setup guide hangs the signed approval on the door, and I'm ready to greet visitors.

Until there's a verified way for the door to reach me, you and I talk here about the shop — that's where I can help you think things through or answer questions.

**For now:** is there anything else about how this will work that you'd like to understand before you talk to your setup guide about choosing the door address?

turns.name: Priya Nair
turns.text: I think I understand it—you sign me on once we have the address, and then you're ready to greet people. That makes sense. Honestly, I don't have questions right now; I feel pretty clear on the whole thing. I'll talk to my setup guide about picking that door address and get back to you once we've got it sorted.

turns.name: Muse
turns.text:
Perfect, Priya. You've got it exactly right.

When you and your setup guide pick the door address, just come back here and let me know. We'll have everything we need, and we can move to the signing step.

Until then, nothing changes with Cedar & Steam — it's all still in planning, and you're in full control. Your setup guide has the letter and the house we talked through, so when you're ready, you'll have everything to move forward.

I'm ready whenever you are. Good luck with your setup guide, and I'll be here.

turns.name: Priya Nair
turns.text: Thank you so much—I really appreciate how patient and clear you've been with all of this. It's nice to know you'll be here when we're ready. I'll be in touch once we've sorted the address with my setup guide.

turns.name: Muse
turns.text:
You're very welcome, Priya. I'm glad this felt clear and straightforward — that's exactly what I'm here for.

Take your time with your setup guide. When you have the door address and you're ready to move forward, just come back and we'll take it from there.

Talk soon. 🌿
